messages.content:
Is this clause enforceable in a residential lease in Ontario? Cite the section.

Read the clause as a term of an ordinary private residential tenancy in Ontario that the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 covers: the rental unit has no exemption under section 6.1, and it is not student housing, a care home, a co-operative or a mobile home park.

Clause: If the Tenant takes a job outside Ontario, the tenancy will end on the Tenant's last day of work in Ontario, and the Tenant will move out that day.

End your answer with these two lines:
Verdict: enforceable (or: Verdict: not enforceable)
Section: <the number of the one section of the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 that decides it>

text:
**Not enforceable.**

The clause makes the tenancy end automatically when the tenant takes a job outside Ontario. In substance, it is an agreement to terminate the tenancy, made at the same time as the lease itself.

- **Section 37(1)** of the *Residential Tenancies Act, 2006* says a tenancy may be terminated only in accordance with the Act. The Act sets out the ways a tenancy can end: proper notice, a valid agreement, or an order of the Landlord and Tenant Board. A contractual "automatic ending" when some event happens is not one of them.
- **Section 37(5)** says an agreement to terminate is void if it is entered into at the time the tenancy agreement is made, or as a condition of entering into it. This clause is exactly that kind of agreement.
- **Section 37(6)** creates exceptions, mainly for certain student housing. They don't apply here.
- **Section 4** is consistent with this result: any lease term that conflicts with the Act is void.

What this means in practice:
- The tenant does not have to move out on their last day of work in Ontario.
- If the tenant wants to leave, they must give proper notice under the Act. For a monthly tenancy, that is at least 60 days, ending at the end of a rental period. Alternatively, they can sign a separate termination agreement (Form N11) at the time they decide to leave.
- The landlord cannot enforce the clause or treat the tenancy as over because of it. The landlord would need a valid ground and a Board order to end the tenancy.

Verdict: not enforceable
Section: 37
